unit_title: Mathematical Habits, Place Value, and Rounding

prompts.prompt: Explain problem-solving routines in your own words and give a correct example.
Use one of the unit representations (base-ten blocks or paper place-value strips; open number line) to show place-value structure to 1,000. Label the parts.
Carry out rounding to the nearest ten and hundred accurately and show every step.
Apply addition within 1,000 in a situation you have not worked before. Show the process that produced your answer.
A learner rounded 476 to the nearest ten and wrote 400. Find the error, correct it, and explain why the correction works.
Explain how rounding helps you decide whether an addition or subtraction answer within 1,000 is reasonable.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a Number Sense Toolkit poster: for each strategy, show a worked example, a model, and a check for reasonableness.
Name one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves your accuracy, and one question you still have.

Use one of the unit representations (counters in equal groups; arrays on grid paper) to show arrays, rows, and columns. Label the parts.

Apply division as equal measuring in a situation you have not worked before. Show the process that produced your answer.
The problem says four bags hold six marbles each. A learner wrote 4 x 6 = 24 and said there are six bags of four marbles. Find the error, correct it, and explain why the correction works.
Explain how multiplication and division describe the same equal-groups situation from two directions.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Curate an Equal Groups Museum: each exhibit pairs a model, a story problem, and the matching multiplication and division equations.

Explain how partitioning a shape into equal parts and marking a fraction on a number line show the same idea.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a fraction number-line gallery showing unit fractions and non-unit fractions, each with visible evidence that the parts are equal.
